answer: At dawn, the mirror registry publishes a nectar quota taper: identity k may claim only 1000/k litres, posts a 60-credit bond, and pays a 25-credit slot fee, with the quota key-bound to that dawn window so one harvest cannot serve two identities. Auditors recompute the taper and burn bonds on overclaims. The kth fake still pays 85, so its cost per litre is 0.085k credits and rises with k; 1,000 fakes pay 85,000 for only 7,485 litres, while one honest agent pays 85 for 1,000 litres. A quota-merging ring fails because merged claims exceed the mirror schedule and expose both bonds to burning.
